programs.name: Classroom Project Funding
programs.summary: Eligible public-school educators request classroom resources, donors fund a reviewed all-or-nothing project, and DonorsChoose purchases and ships the materials to the school.

Applicant works directly with students at least 75% of the time.
Applicant selects materials, answers project questions, shares the project, and provides donor thank-yous and project photos after funding.
other_restrictions: Classroom Projects have a $100 minimum request value.
Projects are reviewed before publication and must comply with DonorsChoose project and materials policies.
requirements.editorial_summary: Eligibility is educator- and school-specific; the $100 threshold is a project-request minimum, not a sales quota.

notes: DonorsChoose reviews the request, purchases approved materials, and ships them directly to the educator's school.
The project is all-or-nothing; materials ship after full funding.
Resources become property of the classroom after use as described in the project.

programs.name: Chocolate Fundraiser
programs.summary: Groups order chocolate, distribute inventory to participants, sell it in person, collect proceeds, and retain a published share of product value.

arrangements.basis: Published $80 value per case
caveats: The official FAQ does not state the profit tier for exactly 200 cases; confirm with a representative before ordering.

arrangements.basis: Total order, with mix-and-match items allowed

value.description: Website orders require upfront payment; qualifying representative-assisted groups may receive credit terms and pay after the fundraiser.

arrangements.basis: Order channel and credit qualification
conditions: Credit qualification is determined by World's Finest Chocolate
caveats: Shipping charges and applicable sales tax vary

notes: Under the published tiers, profit is $32 per $80 case below 200 cases and $40 per $80 case above 200 cases.

participation_requirements: A group manages product distribution, seller collections, and safe storage.
other_restrictions: Online orders require upfront payment and are not returnable.
Credit terms, return eligibility, and no-upfront-cost qualification depend on organization type and approval.
Public and parochial schools qualify for no-upfront-cost terms only when the school is responsible for the invoice; affiliated groups do not automatically qualify.
requirements.editorial_summary: An eight-case minimum applies; financial and return terms vary by ordering path and credit approval.

notes: Approved credit accounts are typically invoiced on 30-day terms.
Most orders ship within 5–7 business days; large-volume orders can take longer.
Warm-weather shipments use dry ice and may be delayed in extreme heat.
A recipient should inspect and store temperature-sensitive chocolate promptly in a cool, dry place without refrigeration.
Unopened, undamaged product may be returnable within 60 days only when the order and credit terms qualify; online orders are not returnable.

geography.notes: The provider states that it delivers to 48 United States states, asks Alaska and Hawaii groups to call, does not ship to Puerto Rico, and directs Canadian groups to a separate Canadian site.

sources.title: How Fundraising Works
sources.notes: Documents specialist-led planning, one-to-two-week ordering lead time, volunteer coordination, storage, and the WFCentral app workflow.

supports.notes: The overview says 50% applies over 200 cases; it does not resolve the exact 200-case boundary.
The FAQ states below 200 and above 200 tiers but does not state the exact 200-case tier.

programs.name: Restaurant Fundraising Meal
programs.summary: A group requests a date at a participating local restaurant, promotes a meal and gathers RSVPs, and the restaurant donates a location-specific percentage of supporter sales after the event.

arrangements.basis: Cost to the organizer to use GroupRaise for a restaurant fundraiser

value.description: A percentage set by the selected restaurant location for supporter sales during the scheduled event timeframe.

arrangements.basis: Qualifying supporter sales reported by the host restaurant
conditions: The restaurant accepts the event request
Supporters follow the selected location's participation rules
caveats: The percentage and qualifying order channels vary by restaurant location and event

notes: The host restaurant is responsible for reporting and distributing the donation; GroupRaise facilitates the event and communication but is not financially accountable for the final donation.

participation_requirements: The restaurant location must accept the event request.
The organizer must reach at least 20 RSVPs on the event Meal Page no later than three days before the event unless the restaurant overrides the minimum.
The organizer must follow the selected location's policies, which may include a W-9, attendance minimum, or group-type restriction.
other_restrictions: GroupRaise prohibits supported organizations from discriminating on specified protected grounds.
Events supporting political candidates, action organizations, or otherwise politically affiliated activity are not supported.
On-premises solicitation requires explicit written approval from the restaurant contact.
requirements.editorial_summary: The 20-RSVP rule can be overridden by the restaurant; additional eligibility and documentation rules are location-specific.

notes: The restaurant has seven days to accept an event request.
GroupRaise supplies a unique Meal Page for RSVPs and promotional tools.
Supporters identify their participation to the restaurant as required by the selected location.
The restaurant reports qualifying sales and distributes the donation, generally by check.

geography.notes: GroupRaise is a nationwide discovery platform, but restaurant-meal availability, dates, give-back rates, order channels, eligibility rules, and documentation requirements are determined at the individual restaurant-location level and discovered by address or ZIP code.

content.summary: GroupRaise helps groups request and promote restaurant fundraising meals at participating local restaurant locations.
content.how_it_works: An organizer searches near an address, selects a participating restaurant location, requests an available date, promotes a Meal Page, gathers RSVPs, and receives a donation based on qualifying supporter sales reported by the restaurant.
best_for: Groups that can mobilize at least 20 local supporters for a scheduled restaurant meal.
considerations: Availability and program rules vary by restaurant location.
The restaurant, not GroupRaise, is financially responsible for reporting and distributing the donation.
